Design 2026-11-26 09:40 UTC (basicly-orch, Orchestrator order; not built). File: .basicly/core/kit/tracker/vault_commit_hook.py, function _judge, called by check().
1. Refuse. When the vault was reached, the commit names a record R, the session is known, and R's holder is not (writer, session), the hook exits REFUSED (1). This covers R held by another session, R held by nobody, and R unknown to the vault fold. The refusal names R, the holder it found (writer and session, or 'nobody'), the session this hook used, and the claim command 'claim R --vault URL'. For R held by another session it also names 'unassign R --take' as the deliberate takeover.
2. Keep accepting with a warning, because refusing would block work that is correct: (a) a claim of this session for R is still queued (unsettled, not yet in the vault); (b) the vault was not reached, which is the existing miss path that records a miss event; (c) Record: none, a git merge subject, and the Revert/fixup/squash echoes, which are exempt as today.
3. Exception for the lander's merge commit. When git_dir/MERGE_HEAD exists (the --no-ff merge of merge.py and the staged-conflict commit after it), the hook accepts R if the vault fold knows R, whatever its holder, because the lander lands another session's lane. The git dir is the parent of the message file (COMMIT_EDITMSG); in a worktree that is .git/worktrees/NAME, where MERGE_HEAD also lives. An unknown R in a merge is still refused. The report carries "exempt": "merge-head".
4. Unknown session (no --session, BASICLY_TRACKER_SESSION, ORCH_SESSION_ID or CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID): keep the warning, plus a line naming the variable to set. This is a hand commit outside an agent, and it cannot be judged. Decision for the Orchestrator; recommended: warn. Failure mode: an agent that runs with no session id at all still passes.
5. One rule: the session name comes from vault_session.session_of (basicly-uyptirb), so the hook and the claim cannot disagree. yeicxzy therefore lands after uyptirb.
Tests (extend tests/test_git_hooks/test_tracker_commit_msg_vault.py; search it first): a commit by session s2 on R held by s1 is refused and names s1 and 'unassign R --take'; an unclaimed R is refused; a queued unsettled claim is accepted with the warning; an unreachable vault is accepted with a miss; a commit with MERGE_HEAD present on R held by s1, by lander session s3, is accepted with exempt merge-head; the same with an unknown R is refused; no session at all gives the warning. Each refusal test fails on the base commit.
Risk: a consumer pinned to an older kit runs the old hook until its next install (consumer hooks run the released basicly), so the gate reaches consumers one release later.

PATH: env BASICLY_USAGE_SNAPSHOT if set, else $XDG_STATE_HOME/basicly/usage-snapshot.json (XDG_STATE_HOME default ~/.local/state); on Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\basicly\usage-snapshot.json. One file per user. A writer computes the path itself; no basicly needed.
JSON: {"format":"basicly.usage-snapshot","version":1,"writer":"orch-statusline-tap"|"handily-board","written_at":<int epoch s UTC>,"windows":{"five_hour":W,"seven_day":W}}
W = {"used_percentage":<number 0-100, from rate_limits.<window>.used_percentage>,"resets_at":<int epoch s, from rate_limits.<window>.resets_at; handily converts resetsAt ISO to epoch s>,"read_at":<int epoch s of this reading>,"readings":[[<epoch s>,<percent>],...]}. A window absent from the input keeps its old object.
READINGS: per window, oldest first, at most 360. Start a new list when resets_at moves by more than 600 s or the percent falls below the last reading. Replace the last reading when it is less than 60 s old, else append.
WRITE: read the old file (ignore it when unreadable or version != 1), merge, write a temp file in the same folder, then os.replace / rename over the path (atomic). Write on every new reading; last writer wins.
VERSION: "version" integer; a reader refuses any other value by name.
STALE: a reader takes now - windows.five_hour.read_at; over 600 s means stale and orch pace refuses.
PLAN: burn rate = (last% - first%) / hours over readings of the last 60 min; needs at least 2 readings spanning 15 min, else unknown. projected_at_reset = used + rate * hours to resets_at. Advice from five_hour: unknown rate -> hold; projected >= 100 or used >= 95 -> close idle; 90 <= projected < 100 -> hold; projected < 90 -> start. seven_day adds a cap: used >= 98 -> close idle, used >= 90 -> hold at most. The final word is the more cautious of the two.

- argv adds --allow-tool 'write(<lane>/**)' with the absolute lane path, so writes outside the lane still ask and, headless, are denied.
- Shell: a short allow list per verb that a lane needs: shell(git status), shell(git diff), shell(git add), shell(git commit), shell(uv run), shell(pytest).
- --deny-tool 'shell(git push)', 'shell(git reset)', 'shell(git checkout)', 'shell(rm)', 'url'. Deny rules win over every allow.

- Claude stays on --permission-mode acceptEdits; Codex stays on -s workspace-write. Each adapter reports its permission ceiling as a capability flag (T3 Y3).
(b) The real Codex usage-limit text.
- When codex exits non-zero, orch delegate saves stdout and stderr to the orch store under delegations/failures/<stamp>.json, as a fixture.
- The first real usage-limit capture becomes a replay fixture in tests (T3 Y2). LIMIT and RESET are then fitted to that exact text, and the generic pattern stays only as a fallback, marked as unfitted in the code test.

(c) The orchestrator delegates read-only research.
- orch delegate --read-only: Claude --permission-mode plan; Codex -s read-only; Copilot with no write or shell allow rules. The lane is not created; the agent runs in the repository root, read-only.
- A tier map in the orch store names the cheapest model per agent (haiku, gpt-6-luna, mai-code-2-flash, sourced 2026-11-26). orch delegate takes --tier cheap, so the Orchestrator never names a model id.
- The orch ruleset gets one rule: research that reads code or docs goes through orch delegate --read-only on the cheapest tier, not a subagent. orch errors counts both, so the saving is measured.
- Order: claude first; codex when it is not at its limit; copilot when the others are at their limit.
(d) From T3 Code and deepseek.
- Takes T3 Y1: capability flags read by the code (names_session, edits, read_only, approval channel). It refuses a missing capability by name.
- Takes T3 Y2: replay fixtures recorded from the real CLI, beside one live smoke turn per agent per release.

JSON: {"format":"basicly.usage-snapshot","version":1,"writer":"handily-board","written_at":<epoch s>,"windows":{"five_hour":W,"seven_day":W}}; W = {"used_percentage":0-100,"resets_at":<int epoch s>,"read_at":<int epoch s of newest accepted reading>,"readings":[[epoch s, percent],...] oldest first, max 360}.
MERGE into your own file, per window: (1) drop a reading whose resets_at <= now; (2) new window object when the stored one is invalid, its resets_at <= now, or resets_at moved forward > 600 s; (3) drop when resets_at moved back > 600 s, percent < stored percent, or time < newest stored reading; (4) else append; if the reading before the newest is < 60 s older than the new one, the new one replaces the newest. A dropped reading does not touch read_at. A window absent from the input keeps its stored object. No change, no write. A file that does not parse counts as empty.
WRITE: in place is allowed (your plan). The Python tap still uses temp + rename, because Claude Code can kill a status line run mid-write.
READ: list *.json; skip a file that does not parse, has another format or version, a writer field not equal to its stem, no five_hour, or five_hour read_at older than 600 s. Per window take the kept object with the latest resets_at, then highest used_percentage, then newest read_at. A torn file costs one skipped file, never a wrong number. My reader needs no retry.
PLAN: five_hour rate = (last% - first%)/hours over readings of the last 60 min, needs 2 readings spanning >= 15 min; else window average used% / hours since (resets_at - 5 h), needs >= 30 min of window; seven_day always window average, needs >= 24 h of window; else rate unknown = 0. projected = used + rate * hours to resets_at. Per window: projected >= 100 or used >= 95 -> close idle; projected >= 90 -> hold; else start. A window with resets_at <= now -> start. Overall = most careful (close idle > hold > start).

[spec v1 FINAL 2026-11-26, from basicly-pace, lane harness/pace-snapshot head 8a8f1fc4, docs/design/usage-snapshot.md; replaces the draft] FOLDER: BASICLY_USAGE_SNAPSHOT_DIR, else XDG_STATE_HOME/basicly/usage-snapshots/ (absolute XDG_STATE_HOME only, else ~/.local/state); Windows LOCALAPPDATA/basicly/usage-snapshots/. JSON: format basicly.usage-snapshot, version 1, writer, written_at epoch s, windows five_hour and seven_day, each used_percentage 0-100, resets_at int epoch s, read_at epoch s of the newest accepted reading, readings [epoch s, percent] oldest first, max 360. MERGE per window: 1 drop a reading whose resets_at is at or before now; 2 new window object when the stored one is invalid, its resets_at is at or before now, or resets_at moved forward more than 600 s; 3 drop when resets_at moved back more than 600 s, the percent is below the stored percent, or the time is before the newest stored reading; 4 else append, and when the reading before the newest is under 60 s older than the new one, the new one replaces the newest. PLAN: five_hour rate over readings of the last 60 min with 2 readings spanning 15 min or more; else the window average used percent per hour since resets_at minus 5 h, with 30 min or more of window; seven_day always the window average with 24 h or more of window; else rate 0. projected = used + rate * hours to resets_at. payload.text:
Plan for basicly-18mhacz, the new basicly workflow (2026-11-26; inputs: tracker-friction-2026-11-21.md, lessons 2026-11-21, landing-timings.json)
Measured today: 19 landings, 11 merged, 8 refused (4 engine-change reruns, 3 flaky wall-clock tests, 1 rebase conflict).
A merged landing took 321 s on average, 306 s of it CI. One serial lander: 11 x 321 s is about 59 min of lock.
About 35 review+confirm pairs today; 14 delivered records could not close; a superseded close is impossible.
REMOVE
1. Per-record review and confirm for task and bug (friction 3,4,14,15,24,37,42,44). Close takes a reason plus the cut's landing evidence.
2. One landing per record. A day-sized cut carries several records and lands once, with one CI proof (owner rule 11).
3. The NOT-READY rerun when a lane changes the engine (4 of 19 today). The lander reruns itself from the lane engine.
4. The held-record need of consumer-proof (basicly-cmb6gqh); a scratch-only proof record.
5. Lost base of a stacked lane (basicly-l9pnzhq): the lander retargets it.
6. Wall-clock bounds in tests as a class (basicly-timing list): bound by the deadline under test, never the runner.
KEEP, with reason
- CI green on the exact commit: the only merge proof that runs where users run (owner keep).
- Consumer proof before a release: it is the only end-to-end install check (owner keep).
- Secret scan and tracker-path-scan: ndlzlv6 shows the queue can carry a user name.
- module-size and complexity gates: local, under 1 s, and they split two modules today.
- Owner-only destruction, "bypassed is never passed", tutorial walk, macOS on push (owner keep).
- Confirm with run evidence for release records only: a release is a promise to users.
CHANGE
- Live state: the lander and claim write orch state per step (orch_note exists), so the board shows step and age.
- No time boxes: drop --wait limits; a long run checkpoints its state and resumes (owner rule 13).
- Landing throughput: workers land their own cut through one merge queue; the queue, not a session, serialises.
FIRST CUT (one day, one lane, build after the owner agrees)
- Tracker: close of a task or bug accepts the landing-verification artifact (commit, CI run URL) as its
  confirmation, and review is no longer required for task and bug. Epic and release keep the full ceremony.
- Superseded close: close --superseded-by RECORD-OR-TAG, checked to exist, no confirmation.
- Proof: replay today's 14 sweep records; each closes in one call. Tracker calls per record drop from 4-6 to 2
  (claim, close), counted from the tracker event log before and after.
Risks: a close by landing evidence can close a record whose criteria the cut did not cover. Control: the close
names the criteria and the cut's test files; a criterion with no test is listed as unchecked in the close reason.
Not decided here: whether workers land themselves (needs the owner's word on the single-writer rule).

payload.title: setup keeps the orch-statusline-tap wrapper in the Claude status line command

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
An existing statusLine command that contains statusline.sh and is not one of the plain forms written by setup stays unchanged after setup, on the host path and in the WSL script.
With orch-statusline-tap on PATH and no wrapper, setup writes "if command -v orch-statusline-tap ><redacted:posix-absolute-path> 2>&1; then exec orch-statusline-tap -- bash ~/.claude/statusline.sh; else exec bash ~/.claude/statusline.sh; fi".
Without orch-statusline-tap on PATH and no wrapper, setup writes the plain form as before.
docs/user-guide.md and docs/what-gets-installed.md describe the rule.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context
When the owner runs "terminal update", setup rewrites the statusLine command in ~/.claude/settings.json to the plain "bash ~/.claude/statusline.sh" (terminal_setup/configs.py, _claude_statusline_command, deploy_claude_statusline and the WSL jq script). On 2026-11-26 at 11:19 UTC setup v0.26.0 removed the orch-statusline-tap wrapper that the owner approved, so basicly usage pacing got no readings. Outcome: setup keeps a wrapper around statusline.sh, and writes the wrapped form when orch-statusline-tap is on PATH.

## Confirmation Plan
Unit tests in tests/test_terminal_setup/test_configs.py for the host path and the WSL shell script: an existing wrapper is kept; with orch-statusline-tap on PATH and no wrapper, setup writes the wrapped form; without it, the plain form. CI green on the landing commit.

Today orch pace says only start, hold or close idle, orch status shows no time since a session's last request, and nothing sends the keep-alive. Supersedes basicly-j8zezq0.

- .basicly/core/kit/orch/orch_pace (advice count, 10 to 30 minute rate)
- .basicly/core/kit/orch/orch_state (request time from the reporter hook, status column, needed mark)

Measured today: 14 lane landings on main (git log --first-parent). Three sessions wrote basicly through lanes (basicly, basicly-orch, basicly-agents). Three landings I timed took 336-438 s, of which local verify was 313-420 s; CI then ran again on the candidate.

1. Jobs lanes do today
- J1 isolation: parallel sessions edit separate checkouts.
- J2 proof: CI green on the exact commit before main moves, with one writer of main.
- J3 cleanup: remove the merged worktree and branch.
- J4 tracker separation: keep tracker writes out of code commits. Vault mode already does this.
2. Simplest form of each job
- J1: a plugin "workspace" with adapters none (one session edits in place), branch (git switch) and worktree (plain git worktree add). basicly adds only the path rule and the venv copy.
- J2: a plugin "delivery" with adapters direct (staged verify, then push; for one-person repos), pr (branch, PR, required CI checks, "require up to date"), and queue (GitHub merge queue on merge_group). Both pr and queue prove the exact merged tree. basicly keeps one piece: a step that writes the landing-verification artifact from the green run on the merged commit (absorbs oov1ouu).
- J3: GitHub deletes the head branch on merge. "basicly clean" removes worktrees whose branch git branch --merged origin/main lists. It keeps the existing condition 3 (no unmerged work is deleted).
- J4: drop it from lanes. Vault mode owns it.
- Gates that stay: commit-msg, pre-commit staged verify, the pre-push local_only record checks (mndj4dz moves there), required CI checks, close --landed.
3. Dropped
- landing.lock and the landing seat. The queue or "require up to date" serializes main.
- The base metadata json, stacked-lane base handling, the CI ref push and dispatch, the rerun from the lane engine (CI runs the candidate's own engine), the lane size ceiling, the preserved artifacts, and the local full verify before a landing.
4. Migration, no lost work
- Step 1: keep basicly worktree merge as adapter delivery=lander, the default. Add pr. Each step is one record and one landing.
- Step 2: the Orchestrator decides branch protection and the merge queue on basicly, because it is a CI/CD setting (ask first).
- Step 3: switch the default to pr or queue after every open lane has landed with the old tool. A lane branch is deleted only when its commits are on origin/main. harness/codex-vault-unsettled stays with its bundle.
- Step 4: retire the lander code after 14 days with no use.
- Risk: the merge queue may be unavailable to a repository owned by a user account, not an organization. This is unverified; check with interface-facts before step 2. If it is unavailable, pr with "require up to date" is the fallback.

payload.value:
## Context
v1 plan (a) on basicly-qpr2xmr.4, cut 3 of 3. orch delegate runs copilot with -p --silent and no permission rules, so in a -p run every edit prompt is denied and copilot cannot work in a lane at all. The workspace rule forbids --allow-all and --yolo. Copilot 1.0.116 (copilot help permissions, read 2026-11-26) takes --allow-tool and --deny-tool patterns; deny wins over every allow, a path write rule scopes edits, and a prompt in a -p run is denied. So a lane write rule, a short shell allow list and deny rules let copilot edit only its lane. The lists live in the adapter as data.

payload.description:
## Context

Step 1 of the basicly-18mhacz cut 2 design, accepted by the Orchestrator. Lanes become a workspace plugin and a delivery plugin. This step adds a pr delivery adapter beside the current lander, which stays the default. It removes no gate. The merge queue is not available for a repository owned by a user account, so pr uses required checks with "require branches up to date".

## Scope

- the delivery adapter seam in basicly worktree merge
- a pr adapter: push the lane branch, open or reuse a pull request with gh, wait for its required checks, merge it, write the landing-verification artifact for the merged commit
- docs and a changelog fragment
payload.requirements:
- gh calls go through the existing adapter module; no new subprocess site.
- A refused push or a failed check names its cause and lands nothing.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
The pr adapter counts failed landing-workflow runs on every earlier pull request head of the lane whose tree equals the candidate's outside the ledger, and refuses before any push when that count exceeds the rerun limit.
A candidate head that already has a failed or non-first-attempt run is refused before any push, with a cause that says a retry needs a new head and names the commands that give one.
A head whose tree failed once gets one more run on a new head, so a flaky failure can be retried once with git commit --allow-empty or a rebase.
payload.description:
## Context

Found on 2026-11-26 when basicly-18mhacz.1 failed on pull request 11 (run 45849583517). The pr adapter counted failed runs only on the exact head, while the lander counts every head with the same tree outside the ledger (ci_landing.failed_runs with the tried heads of ci-proofs.json). So a new empty commit could dodge the rerun limit. A push of the same head starts no new pull_request run, and gh run rerun makes attempt 2, which the first-attempt rule refuses; the adapter then waits on the old failed run and refuses with a cause that does not say how to retry.

## Scope

- src/basicly/delivery_pr.py
- tests/test_delivery_pr.py
- .basicly/core/skills/worktree-isolation/references/lifecycle.md and its projections
- changelog.d/

The pr adapter reads the earlier pr/NAME/ heads of the lane (gh pr list --state all) and counts failed runs on those with the same tree outside the ledger through ci_landing.failed_runs, as the lander does. A head that already has a failed or rerun-only run is refused before any push, with git commit --allow-empty or a rebase named as the retry; a tree that failed once gets one more run on a new head; a pass only on attempt 2 is refused. 45 tests in the adapter, merge and ci_landing files pass; full pyright 0 errors; staged verify passed. Done before: basicly-5zhdian closed as superseded by basicly-pl4ybu0, evidence copied there; 18mhacz.1 now blocked by 18mhacz.3.

Root cause (root-cause skill): CI 45842501638 and 45849583517 failed because vault_clone.durable wrote whole files through a fixed name <file>.tmp. Two session processes writing view.tried at once share that temporary file; the first replace moves it into place, the second replace raises FileNotFoundError (view.tried.tmp -> view.tried), and that process exits 1. Reproduced deterministically by a second write inside the first fsync; the error text matches CI. Old: lines date from 2026-11-12 (487972c2, decfacab). Local load (10 runs x 2 commits, 4 cores) never reproduced it. Fix in lane harness/pl4ybu0-durable-temp 8dcce51b: per-writer temporary name from events.temporary_beside and cleanup on failure; no bound changed. Not shown: whether the claim-load exit 4 (45832078135) has the same cause.

## Context

Found by the agent that repaired handily-cghnx5 on 2026-11-17 (engine row ref pinned in 120 assertions). Two more engine-owned details are pinned the same way, so a Claude Code update can break the mod or its tests:

1. mods/handily-simple-view/hooks/output.ts:11, shipped code: PERSON_REJECTED_OUTPUT = User rejected tool use, the exact text the engine writes for a person rejection. If the engine changes it, simple-view stops drawing the denied by you row.
2. mods/handily-simple-view/simple-view.test.ts: exact denial and rejection texts captured from given versions (EDIT_DENIED_ON_2_1_296 and BASH_DENIED_ON_2_1_296 at lines 1636-1637, BASH_DENIED_ON_2_1_311 at 1638, FILE_REFUSALS_CAPTURED_ON_2_1_312 at 1649, RULE_DENIED_BASH_ON_2_1_322 at 2118, PERSON_DENIED_ON_2_1_312 at 2120, PERSON_REJECTED_ANSWER_ON_2_1_323 at 2131), and 19 literal engine error strings such as File has not been read yet, File does not exist and has been denied.

Owner rule: an engine update must not break a mod, and tests never pin engine-owned details. Also seen, lower risk: mods/handily-board/agents.test.ts:1497 needs the test kit to raise tool.check for a test tool call; board.test.ts:9712 needs the engine row to be the first child of the rebuilt row.

Finding 2026-11-26: the mod API gives no structured field for a person rejection or a rule denial on Claude Code 2.1.332 (types searched for rejected, denied and decision), and the tool_decision telemetry name is also engine-owned. So the text match stays, and the fix makes an unknown wording fall back to the engine row by test.

## Confirmation Plan

payload.text:
Council question for basicly-18mhacz.6 (draft, basicly-lanes, 2026-11-26 17:00 UTC).
Question: Should close --landed accept, for one criterion of a task or bug, a command argv with its observed result and exit code 0 instead of a test file, so that no follow-up record opens? YES or NO.
Today's rule (cut 1, council 2-1 YES at 12:22 UTC): close --landed needs the landing-verification artifact (CI green on the merge commit) and maps each criterion to a test file in that commit or to null; null opens a follow-up "Add a test" record, and the parent epic cannot close while it is open.
Evidence FOR:
- Measured today: 2 of 7 close --landed calls had a criterion that only a run can prove (a timing stated in a commit body, basicly-18mhacz.4; the tool deleting a real branch, basicly-18mhacz.5). Each opened a follow-up (basicly-beodicq, basicly-7xfolo2) that needed create, review, confirm and close: 4 tracker calls per criterion, the friction cut 1 was meant to remove.
- The follow-up title "Add a test" was wrong for both: a test cannot prove that a real origin branch was deleted or how long a real run took.
- The old confirm path already accepts exactly this shape (criterion, command argv, result, exit code 0), so the evidence form is not new; only its place is.
Evidence AGAINST:
- It opens a second way through the close gate. A test file in the landed commit is checked by git (cat-file in the commit); a command result is text the closer writes, and nothing re-runs it. A closer can claim a result the command never printed.
- The null follow-up is the control that makes an untested criterion visible on the epic; a command entry removes that signal for every criterion a closer chooses to map that way, including ones a test could cover.
- Volume is small (2 criteria today); the cost is 4 calls each, against a permanent widening of the gate.
Possible conditions if YES: only for criteria whose text names a run, a timing or a remote state; the command must be read-only; the close prints the entry so it shows in the record; an epic close lists every command-proved child criterion.
Recommendation: NO for now, keep null and the follow-up, and shorten the follow-up instead: let review and confirm run in one call for a follow-up of type task opened by close --landed. That removes most of the cost without a new way through the gate.

Revised blind brief for the council (Orchestrator edits 2026-11-26 17:00 UTC: no recommendation in the brief; option C added). My own recommendation stays only in the earlier comment.
Council question for basicly-18mhacz.6 (blind brief, 2026-11-26).
Question: How should close --landed treat a criterion of a task or bug that only a run can prove, not a test file? Choose one option, A, B or C, and give your reason.
Today's rule: close --landed needs the landing-verification artifact (CI green on the merge commit) and maps each criterion to a test file in that commit or to null. A null opens a follow-up record titled "Add a test"; the parent epic cannot close while it is open. That follow-up then closes only through review --evidence, confirm --evidence and close: three calls, plus its creation.
Option A, command evidence: close --landed also accepts, per criterion, a command argv with its observed result and exit code 0, and opens no follow-up for it. Conditions: only for a criterion whose text names a run, a timing or a remote state; the command must be read-only; the close prints the entry into the record; an epic close lists every command-proved child criterion.
Option B, keep as is: null and the follow-up stay; nothing changes.
Option C, one-call follow-up: keep null and the follow-up, but a follow-up of type task opened by close --landed may record its review and confirmation in one call instead of two.
Evidence for a change (A or C):
- Measured on 2026-11-26: 2 of 7 close --landed calls in one session had such a criterion (a timing written in a commit body; the tool deleting a real remote branch). Each opened a follow-up that took create, review, confirm and close: about 4 tracker calls per criterion.
- The follow-up title "Add a test" fit neither case: a test cannot show that a real origin branch was deleted or how long a real run took.
- The old confirm path already takes the shape criterion, command argv, result, exit code 0.
Evidence against a change (B):
- A: a test file is checked by git inside the landed commit; a command result is text the closer writes, and nothing re-runs it.
- A: the null follow-up is the signal that shows an untested criterion on the epic; A removes it for each criterion mapped to a command.
- C: it merges two separate steps of the close gate, review (the plan of checks) and confirm (their results), into one call for these follow-ups.
- Volume is small: 2 criteria in one day, against a lasting change to the gate.
Answer format: OPTION: A, B or C. REASON: up to 5 sentences. RISK: the main way your option fails.
